title: Keep Your Game Art on One Style
summary: Turn your game concept into one style guide, then check every new sprite and store graphic against it, so a small studio ships art that looks like one game.

money_potential.label: Medium
money_potential.basis: Assumes you make game art with several people or tools; the value is fewer redraws.
money_potential.note: Value tiers are our rough estimates (labelled Estimate) of relative value to the business, each with its assumption. They are not promises, income claims or advice. Results depend on your market, offer and effort.

how_it_makes_money: Fewer redraws when art from different people or tools does not match.
Store and social graphics that match the game itself.
who_its_for: Indie game studios and solo developers.
Small teams that use AI image tools for art.

stack.name: Game Art Director
stack.role: Writes the style guide, palettes and prompt sheets, slices sprite sheets and checks for drift.
stack.creator: DannyLimanseta

stack.name: Graphic Design Assistant
stack.role: Makes store and social graphics in Canva in the right sizes.
stack.creator: shubgaur

inputs.label: Game concept and references you own

steps.name: Game Art Director
steps.does: Writes the style guide and checks drift

steps: Describe the game and share a few references you own.
Lock the style guide and palettes.
Check each new batch of art for palette and grid drift.
Make store and social graphics from the same guide.
guardrails: Use only references you own or have the right to use.
Check the licence of any AI image tool you use commercially.
